full_judgment:
2. It appears that the Divisional Commissioner had instructed the Deputy Commissioner, Dacca to requisition the main building of the Nalgola Raj Kuthi having 14 rooms only which were in occupation of one Mr. Abdul Quddus, but the Deputy Commissioner, by the impugned order, requisitioned this property along with a different property, being holding No. 47. Roy Iswar Chandra Shil Bahadur Street, Dacca which is a property of Court of Wards and in which 27 other families were directed to be evicted by the Deputy Commissioner in consequence of the requisition. The petitioner challenged this order of requisition by a revisional application filed before the Government of Bangladesh under section 4 of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act. The Government in their order dated 7.1.78, Annexur D, observed that the Deputy Commissioner instead of requisitioning a part of the holding in occupation of one Abdul Quddus requisitioned the entire holding No. 47 which consisted of many other rooms which were in occupation of other persons and that those portions were property of Court of Wards. The Government held that the impugned requisition was unjustified, but the Government instead of exercising their power of revision, forwarded the application for revision to the Divisional Commissioner for disposed, although the Divisional Commissioner has got no power of revision under the Requisition Act. It further appears that the petitioner pointed out this illegality in the Government order but the Government insisted on the revisional application being disposed of by the Divisional Commissioner. The Additional Divisional Commissioner then dealt with the matter. He beard the parties on five occasions, 23.1.78, 7.2.78, 20.3.78, 18.4.78 and 6.5.78 and reserved his judgment till 20.5.78. But on that date, the Additional Divisional Commissioner observed that further time would be necessary for delivery of the Judgment as he was preoccupied with other urgent works and adjourned the case till 13.6.78 for judgment but no judgment was delivered on that date also. The petitioner filed an application on 8.7.78 requesting the Additional Commissioner to pass his judgment but no judgment was announced. In these circumstances the petitioner moved this court alleging, inter alia, malafides on the part of both the Additional Commissioner who was withholding the judgment and the Deputy Commissioner who had passed the order of requisition. 

 3. Mr. M.B. Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioner contends that the order of requisition being malafide and illegal it should be knocked down by this court. Mr. Quazi Shafiuddin, the learned Asstt. Attorney General who appeared for the respondents, has submitted that the matter is sub-judice and as such jurisdiction of this Court should not be exercised in a matter sub-judice. He has tried to explain that the Additional Commissioner could not deliver judgment because of pre-occupation and that the Additional Commissioner, in the meantime, retired from service. 

 4. Whatever may be the reason for undue delay in disposing of such a simple matter, whether this amounts to willful neglect of duty or incompetence of the Additional Commissioner, the order of the Government forwarding the revisional application of the petitioner to the Divisional Commissioner for disposal in it-self found to be illegal since revisional jurisdiction under the Emergency Requisition of Property Act lies only with the Government. The Divisional Commissioner has been given powers or hearing appeal from an order of requisition passed by the Deputy Commissioner, but no appeal can be filed after expiry of a period of 30 days from the date of requisition and this being the position the revision application forwarded to the Commissioner by the Government cannot be treated as an appeal under section 4A of the said Act. Mr. Sharifuddin suggests that a direction may be given by this court upon the Additional Commissioner to dispose of the case by his judgment. This suggestion, if accepted, will cause further damage to the petitioner. For, the order by the Divisional Commissioner passed in revision will be without jurisdiction. Since the Government came to a finding that the requisition in respect of entire holding was unjustified, it was incumbent upon the Government to dispose of the revisional Application by modifying the order of requisition so as to exceed from the requisition the portion which fell to the share of the Court of Wards. We do not think that this matter should drag on further. The order of requisition may be modified here.
